category_title: Struggling readers who view reading as a process of remembering and repeating
minimal_context: Alyssa is participating in a whole-class literacy activity where students are changing letters on a magnet board to make different words in the /an/ family.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Class, let's look at the magnet board. We are going to change the first letter to make different words in the /an/ family.

STUDENT: (Attentively watches the teacher during the group instruction but does not focus on the print on the board.)

TUTOR: Let's read this first word together. The word is 'pan'.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly, silently mouthing the word as it is read by others, continuing to watch the teacher instead of looking at the board.)

TUTOR: Now I am changing the first letter. Alyssa, what should we do to figure out how to read this?

STUDENT: To do it over and over again, 'Cause if you do it over and over again, you’ll know how to read.

options.A: Have the student practice the literacy activity by tracing along the letters on the magnet board with her finger.
options.B: Ask metacognitive questions about the purpose and value of the lesson (e.g., 'Why is what we just learned important?' 'How will this help us to be better readers?')
options.C: Maintain a quiet and relaxing environment during the literacy activity; talk gently and slowly; avoid loud speech.
options.D: Place an exclusive display board in the classroom only for Alyssa to display her word family work.
